scoring_policy.unit: Ranked retrieved chunks, in their original retrieval order.
scoring_policy.query_input: Use only each case.question as the query. Keep all labels, page numbers and expected answers out of the query/context used by the retriever.
scoring_policy.filename_matching: Match canonical source basename exactly after normalizing path separators. If your corpus renames files, create a fixed alias map verified by source SHA-256.
scoring_policy.pdf_page_basis: relevant_pages are 1-based physical PDF positions. Convert confirmed zero-based parser page metadata by adding 1; do not add 1 to metadata already 1-based. printed_pages are for human audit only.
scoring_policy.multiple_pages: Any listed relevant page can independently support the answer (OR, not AND). In retrieval_010, page 6 OR page 8 is sufficient.
scoring_policy.text_location: Customer Service Plan relevant_pages=null means no pagination, not whole-document relevance. Use the named section and evidence paragraph/line. Never invent page 1.
scoring_policy.primary_relevance: Correct source plus answer-bearing passage. Before scoring, bind the verified evidence to actual chunk IDs by inspecting all chunks covering the listed page/section, independently of ranked FAISS output. Accept a chunk only if its text/table context supports the complete requested fact(s). Freeze those qrels before retrieval. This dataset supplies source evidence labels; it does not invent unseen chunk IDs.
scoring_policy.coarse_locator_diagnostic: A correct source and matching page/section can be scored separately as locator Hit@k/MRR. This is a proxy and can count a chunk from the right page that lacks the answer; never label it strict evidence retrieval.
scoring_policy.chunking_limits: If chunking separates facts, qualifiers or table headers so no individual chunk supports the answer, record an evidence-fragmentation issue. Do not silently count partial evidence as a full hit. Top-k combined-evidence coverage can be a separate metric.
scoring_policy.rank_policy: Use original chunk ranks, retaining duplicates unless a separate deduplication policy was fixed before all comparisons. Do not deduplicate to four document names.
scoring_policy.hit_at_k: For k in [1,3,5], each case is 1 if at least one relevant chunk is at rank <= k, else 0. Dataset Hit@k is the mean over all 10 cases.
scoring_policy.mrr: Reciprocal rank is 1/r for the first relevant chunk, else 0 when absent from the evaluated ranking. MRR is the mean over all cases. If only top 5 is retrieved, call the result MRR@5; do not claim untruncated MRR.
scoring_policy.unjudged: Missing source/page metadata or uncertain passage relevance must be logged for review, never automatically counted as correct. An unjudged candidate is not known irrelevant; report any incomplete labeling.
scoring_policy.reporting: Report numerator/10 with Hit@1, Hit@3 and Hit@5; MRR depth; per-case first relevant rank; and per-document-family counts. One case changes aggregate Hit@k by 10 percentage points.
scoring_policy.cost: Once corpus chunks have been mapped to frozen qrels, scoring is deterministic and requires no LLM judge or paid API call.

limitations: Ten cases are a development baseline, not a held-out comprehensive test.
Questions are deliberately source-scoped where needed to avoid ambiguous cross-document relevance.
Source/page labels are verified; corpus-specific chunk relevance IDs must be bound after inspecting the actual indexed chunks.
No retriever was run and no Hit@k/MRR result is claimed.

cases.question: Under Delta's domestic Contract of Carriage, how is an involuntary refund calculated when no part of the ticket has been used?
cases.expected_topic: Involuntary refund amount for a wholly unused ticket
cases.expected_answer: Where an involuntary refund is required under Rule 22(A) and no portion of the ticket has been used, the refund equals the fare paid.
cases.supporting_quote: If no portion of the ticket has been used, the refund will be an amount equal to the fare paid.
cases.why_relevant: The sentence states the calculation requested, under the involuntary-refund heading. The question assumes entitlement and does not ask for all refund-eligibility conditions.
cases.scope_note: Page 15 gives triggering events under Rule 19(A), but is not sufficient evidence for this specific unused-ticket calculation; page 22 discusses voluntary fully refundable tickets.
cases.expected_evidence: Where an involuntary refund is required under Rule 22(A) and no portion of the ticket has been used, the refund equals the fare paid.
cases.verification_method: Direct source reading; PDF evidence pages also rendered and visually inspected. No FAISS or other retrieval result used to establish relevance.
cases.quote_note: Supporting quotations preserve source wording; PDF line breaks and extraction spacing may be cleaned. The DOT quotation is a row transcription and must be read with its column headings.

cases.question: What is the general maximum baggage-liability amount per fare-paying passenger in Delta's domestic Contract of Carriage, excluding wheelchairs and other assistive devices?

cases.expected_answer: The general cap is $4,700 per fare-paying passenger, limited to proven damage or loss. The maximum-liability limitation does not apply to wheelchairs or other assistive devices.

cases.why_relevant: Rule 17(B)(1)(a) states the general cap and unit; 17(B)(3)(a), on the same page, identifies the assistive-device exception.
cases.scope_note: This is a maximum, not an automatic payout. Page 15 repeats $4,700 only in the separate multiple-carrier rule and is not a substitute for the general-rule evidence.

cases.question: For July 2026, what were the on-time arrival percentage and marketing-carrier rank of the Delta Air Lines Network, including its branded codeshare partners, at all U.S. airports?
cases.document_identity: U.S. Department of Transportation, Office of Aviation Consumer Protection, Air Travel Consumer Report, issued September 2026; Flight Delays data for July 2026.
cases.expected_topic: Delta marketing network July 2026 on-time arrival percentage and rank
cases.expected_answer: 71.7% of the Delta Air Lines Network's reported flight operations arrived on time; it ranked 3rd among the reporting marketing carriers for July 2026.

expected_evidence.carrier_scope: Delta Air Lines Network (marketing carrier, including branded codeshare partners)
expected_evidence.footnote_scope: Table 1 footnote 1 includes U.S. airlines with at least 0.5% of total domestic scheduled-service passenger revenues plus branded codeshare partners. Displayed statistics use one decimal place; rankings use nine decimal places.
expected_evidence.distinctions: The 71.9% figure is for Delta-operated mainline flights, not its marketing network. Table 1B's 78.1% and rank 2 are year-to-date, not July.

cases.supporting_description: On page 6, Table 1's network row aligns 211 with Number of Airports Reported, 71.7 with Percent of On-Time Arrivals, and 3 with Rank. Page 8 Table 1B independently repeats 71.7 and rank 3 in the Jul 26 columns of the bold Delta Air Lines marketing-network row.
cases.why_relevant: Either accepted page directly contains both requested July marketing-network values. The explicit network scope and month prevent confusion with the nearby Delta mainline figures or year-to-date columns.
